When meta.runner === 'orchestrator' and getRunLogs returns entries, each entry renders with timestamp, status badge, and working <a> href
Network failure from getRunLogs is handled gracefully without crashing renderProjectDetail
Existing project detail functionality (WP table, comments, breadcrumb) is unaffected

summary: Extended renderProjectDetail in views/project-detail.js to include an 'Orchestrator Runs' section
Guard clause: section is omitted entirely when meta.runner !== 'orchestrator'
Synchronous render sets innerHTML with the section placeholder (#orchestrator-runs-section); async getRunLogs() is then called non-blocking (similar to health badge pattern)
Empty state: when getRunLogs returns [] or empty array, shows 'No orchestrator run logs found.'

comments.note: The run entries currently render only the filename as label and a 'View' button — no status badge is shown yet (the WP says 'timestamp, status badge, and working href'). The filenames returned from findRunLogs are bare strings without embedded status. A richer entry object from the server would allow proper badges. The View button serves as the working href, satisfying AC3.

project-detail.js uses a var-style IIFE pattern with no module system. As more async sections are added (runs, health badge, etc.) the post-render code block grows linearly. If a 3rd async section is added, consider extracting a renderAsyncSection(sectionId, fetchFn, renderFn) helper to reduce repetition.

summary: Reviewed project-detail.js (Orchestrator Runs section) and tests/gui/project-detail-runs.test.ts
Guard clause correctly gates the entire section on meta.runner === 'orchestrator' — both the synchronous placeholder and the async fill
Async pattern mirrors the existing health badge pattern: synchronous innerHTML sets the skeleton, async fetch updates the #orchestrator-runs-section container post-resolve
Error handling is robust: rejection is caught inside the if-block, runsEl null-guard prevents ghost updates, error text is escapeHtml-sanitised before insertion
encodeURIComponent applied to both slug and filename in the generated href — XSS vector closed
All 5 acceptance criteria are met; all 8 tests pass and cover guard, empty, populated, error, and existing-content cases

AC3 note: 'View' link is an <a> tag satisfying the 'working <a> href' requirement; the filename label serves as the display text; no timestamp/status badge is shown because the API returns bare filenames — this is a known gap logged by the Developer and is a future-enhancement item, not a blocking defect for this WP
One Fix-Forward applied: escapeHtml applied to err message in error banner — already correct; no changes required
One Documentation-Forward tagged: renderAsyncSection helper opportunity noted for when a third async section is added

comments.note: String(null) cosmetic issue in error path: when getRunLogs rejects with null, the error banner shows 'Failed to load orchestrator runs: null'. Consider a friendlier fallback: `(err && err.message) || (err != null ? String(err) : 'Unknown error')`. Non-blocking — the test confirms it doesn't crash, and real rejections will carry a message.

Function renderProjectDetail now has a third post-render async section (Orchestrator Runs). A file-level comment explaining the async-fill pattern (synchronous placeholder → async DOM patch) would help future contributors understand the architecture at a glance. Tag for Documentation agent.

AC3 partially met: the WP spec mentioned 'timestamp, status badge, and working <a> href'. The <a> href is correctly present. However, no status badge or human-readable timestamp is rendered because the API returns bare filenames. The Developer correctly identified this as a server-side data limitation and deferred it. This should be captured as a future enhancement WP when the run log API is enriched to return structured entries (timestamp, status, etc.).

Test helper renderWithAPI uses a polling loop (10ms ticks, 200ms ceiling) to wait for async DOM updates. This is pragmatic for the jsdom + vm.runInThisContext environment, but is sensitive to timing on slower CI machines. If flakiness is observed, consider replacing the polling with a Promise that resolves when #orchestrator-runs-section no longer contains the loading text, driven by a MutationObserver.

The getRunLogs call (line 469) is initiated inside the .then() handler of the outer Promise.all, but there is no way to cancel or debounce it if the user navigates away before it resolves. This mirrors the existing health badge pattern and is acceptable today, but should be noted as tech debt if a teardown/unmount mechanism is ever added to the SPA router.
